activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization

feedback.problem: The graph of the function $f(x)$ passes through $(3,6)$ and ${f}^{′}(3)=-5.$ Find $L(x),$ the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the graph of $f(x)$ passes through $(3,6)$, we have that $f(3)=6.$ Therefore, the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $a=3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(3)+{f}^{′}(3)(x-3) \\  & =6-5(x-3) \\  & =6-5x+15 \\  & =-5x+21.\end{aligned}
$$
